newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see Quebec price dollar deal at +58 bp.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see Quebec price dollar deal at +58 bp.

text.p: The primary market saw another active and full day of issuance on Thursday.
Quebec priced its $750 million 10-year global bond to yield 58 basis points over the 6.5 percent October 2006 U.S. Treasury -- the tighter end of the 58 to 60 indicated range.
Joint lead managers for the transaction were Merrill Lynch, CSFB, Goldman Sachs, Nomura and SBC Warburg.
In January last year Quebec launched a $500 million 10-year Yankee bond which was priced to yield 78 b.p. over U.S. Treasuries via Merrill Lynch.
Quebec is rated A2 by Moody's and A+ by S&P.
A syndicate official at Goldman Sachs said the spread had tightened to 57 b.p. over, which proved the success of the transaction.
"We saw very strong demand from outside North America in both Asia and Europe predominantly from institutional investors," he said.
Another syndicate official at Nomura said there had been good Asian and Japanese demand.
"It is a high-yielding transaction...Quebec has not come to the market for some time and it is an improving credit -- they have a good story to tell," he said.
